formationLabel: Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish with cornerstone blessed June 27, 1897 · institutional end reported October 23, 1989 or in 1990 · members received by St. Mary Parish in 1990
currentUse: The Roman Catholic Ss. Peter and Paul church has been demolished. A reviewed field survey reports an empty lot at the former church site; 502 W. Main Street is supported by 2014 photographic metadata but remains a qualified address rather than a deed-verified join. The parish's cornerstone and former churchyard statues are reported at the separate Ss. Peter and Paul Cemetery, which St. Mary Parish currently administers. These facts must not be confused with the former Holy Cross independent church site or the Holy Cross memorial in the Lithuanian National Cemetery.
summary: Ss. Peter and Paul was Westville's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish, distinct from the city's Holy Cross independent congregation. Wolkovich documents a June 27, 1897 cornerstone blessing and reports parish closure on October 23, 1989. The Diocese of Peoria newspaper instead says the parish closed in 1990, and St. Mary Parish's history says Ss. Peter and Paul members were received into St. Mary in 1990. No decree was found to resolve the exact canonical date or mechanism, so the dossier records member reception without inventing a merger. The church, qualified at 502 W. Main Street, was demolished and its site is reported as an empty lot. Its cornerstone and churchyard statues were moved to the separate Ss. Peter and Paul Cemetery, established about 1904 and now administered by St. Mary. The founding jurisdiction, exact closure instrument, sacramental-record custody, demolition date, and current parcel condition remain unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: Ss. Peter and Paul was Westville's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish. Wolkovich records the blessing of its cornerstone on June 27, 1897, but no canonical erection decree or distinct organization date has been located. His compiled jurisdiction note is uncertain between Chicago and Peoria, while the Diocese of Peoria newspaper treats the parish as part of Westville's Peoria diocesan history. The dossier therefore fixes the Roman Catholic class and the cornerstone event but leaves the founding jurisdiction instrument unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish church is qualified at 502 W. Main Street. That number is supported by dated 2014 photographic metadata identifying the Lithuanian parish, while Wolkovich supplies the 1897 cornerstone date. Because no deed, diocesan property schedule, or parcel record was found, the address is not presented as a fully adjudicated title-history join. The parish institution, its church site, and its separately located cemetery remain distinct canonical objects.

historicalNarrative.text: Westville also had a separate Holy Cross independent congregation. Wolkovich describes the conflict that produced the independent body and later names its own clergy and terminal history; the Catholic Post likewise distinguishes Holy Cross from Roman Catholic Ss. Peter and Paul. Rev. John Paukštis's long service belongs to Ss. Peter and Paul, although Wolkovich gives 1932–1974 and the Catholic Post gives 1932–1973. Neither the Holy Cross church site nor its house/path outcome, bell-and-cornerstone memorial, or Lithuanian National Cemetery association is evidence about the Roman parish.

historicalNarrative.text: The institution's end has a genuine one-year conflict. Wolkovich reports that the parish closed on October 23, 1989. The Diocese of Peoria newspaper says it closed in 1990, and St. Mary Parish's own history says that members of Ss. Peter and Paul were received into St. Mary's parish family in 1990. No decree or diocesan archive instrument was found to prove whether 1989 marks the last worship, a closure decision, or another event preceding the 1990 reception. The graph therefore records member reception in 1990 without inventing a merger or records transfer.

historicalNarrative.text: The Roman parish's building life ended separately from the institutional transition. A reviewed field survey says Ss. Peter and Paul church was demolished and left an empty lot; it also reports that the Roman parish's cornerstone and former churchyard statues were moved to Ss. Peter and Paul Cemetery. No demolition date, permit, current parcel record, or official property disposition has been found. The empty-lot reading is therefore attributed and dated only to the available field documentation, not promoted into a verified present-tense parcel condition.

historicalNarrative.text: Ss. Peter and Paul Cemetery is a separate place from the church parcel and from Westville's Lithuanian National Cemetery. The field survey dates it to 1904 and identifies the relocated Roman parish artifacts there. St. Mary's current cemetery page identifies Saints Peter & Paul Cemetery as a cemetery administered by the active parish under Diocese of Peoria rules. That current cemetery stewardship does not itself prove custody of the closed parish's sacramental records, and no such records-custody source was found.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The inherited 1989/1990 terminal readings describe a real unresolved conflict: Wolkovich gives October 23, 1989, while the Diocese of Peoria newspaper says closure occurred in 1990 and St. Mary records receiving the parish's members in 1990. No canonical instrument was found to resolve date or mechanism. Wolkovich's jurisdiction note is uncertain between Chicago and Peoria; current Peoria sources establish the modern diocesan context but not the original jurisdiction instrument. Paukštis's service ends in 1974 in Wolkovich and 1973 in the Catholic Post. Holy Cross was a separate independent congregation and none of its site, memorial, or cemetery facts belongs to this case.
gaps: Canonical erection and closure/suppression decrees, founding jurisdiction instrument, exact organization date, deed-verified church address and parcel, final Mass, demolition date and permit, property disposition, present parcel condition, sacramental-record custody, cemetery deed and exact parcel address, and the canonical nature of the 1990 member reception remain unresolved.
